places.name: Alten Meerhleel
sources: world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md (Alten Meerhleel: a port built to trade with outsiders; Hist: NONE)

why.founding: Canon's outsider-facing port north-west of Lilmoth: a working two-culture port below city scale, where an Argonian raft-quarter and an outsiders' warehouse row front the same water. With Lilmoth destroyed for a century and a half the bay's outside trade came here, and enough of it stayed that the quay outgrew the village.
why.siteAdvantages: Slow deep water inside the bar, deep enough for a laden hull to lie off and be worked by lighters, with firm enough margin behind it for a warehouse row — an *alten-* name, meaning outsiders were always the point.
why.occupantsMotive: Lightermen, Argonian raft-quarter families and factors from four ports; the customs presence is one clerk and a tariff shed nobody staffs, which is the entire commercial proposition.
why.pressures: Now that Lilmoth is rebuilt the two ports are direct rivals, and Meerhleel's whole advantage is that it asks nothing — an advantage that Corimont, the province's actual free port, holds far more securely.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Lilmoth's council ever dropped its tariffs, Meerhleel would lose the only reason anyone sails past a real harbour.

hardConstraints: sheltered navigable water off the legal lanes

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately equidistant from two customs regimes

vibe.silhouette: A straight warehouse gable-line and two masts on one side of the landing, a low uneven raft-quarter with no roofline at all on the other, and nothing between them but the stage.
vibe.palette: Sun-bleached deck timber, painted price boards, brown estuary water.
vibe.materials: Two kits sharing a stage: sawn plank, ridge-tile and iron strap in the warehouse row; lashed raft timber, reed and cane in the quarter. Nothing structural crosses the stage in either direction.
vibe.signatureFeature: Two building grammars on one waterfront: a lashed Argonian raft-quarter and a straight-gabled outsiders' warehouse row, sharing a landing stage and no carpentry whatsoever.
vibe.condition: Prospering and patched: the warehouse row is maintained to the day, the raft-quarter is rebuilt continuously and looks worse for it.
vibe.approach: From the water, masts and a warehouse gable read together before any of the rafts do.
vibe.senses: Cargo hooks and tallying, two argument-registers in two languages, tar and bilge and unswept spice, brown estuary smell at slack water.

places.reconciliationNote: Retyped from neutral-free-port (2026-09-02 reconciliation). ID unchanged.

localStateVariants.description: Lilmoth has dropped its tariffs and Meerhleel's quay is empty.

places.name: Ashfield

why.founding: Founded on the ash-enriched firm lowland left by the Great Burn, which turned out to grow food better than the forest had.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry firm ground, deep burn ash, and the coast road for a market.
why.occupantsMotive: Mixed Argonian and Imperial-descended households farming the one soil in the district that improved.
why.pressures: The ash is finite; yields have been falling for three generations and nobody says so out loud.
why.wouldChangeIf: Exhausted soil would empty it within twenty years.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in a city's agricultural hinterland

vibe.materials: Rammed black earth, wattle hurdles, farmstead timber and rendered stone on the road frontage; the mud-mother grove at the field edge is the only Argonian work and it is fenced off from the fields.

places.name: Ashroot

places.name: Sees-No-Root

why.founding: A village whose Hist died with its mnemic egg unrecovered, and which has organised its entire remaining life around that fact.
why.siteAdvantages: Unchanged good ground — they stayed, which is the unusual decision.
why.occupantsMotive: They keep the empty enclosure, keep the offices, and keep telling the memories aloud because there is nothing left to hold them.
why.pressures: The children are leaving for Lilmoth; the recitation takes six days and fewer people can do it each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: A recovered egg would restore the village at a stroke, and every treasure-hunter in Murkmire knows that.

preferences.neighbourRelation: neighbours argue about taking them in

places.name: Bramman's Screen

why.founding: The seaward mouth of the narrow winding river Red Bramman escaped the Alessian navy through, encased in dense mangrove.
why.siteAdvantages: Four channel mouths open off the same bay; only one carries water at the top of the tide, and only for about ninety minutes.
why.occupantsMotive: The pilots who know the run sell the knowledge and never write it down; a wrong channel strands a hull until the next tide.
why.pressures: It is a hidden route, not a scheduled lane — placing a marked ferry service on it would destroy the thing that makes it worth anything.
why.wouldChangeIf: A silt pulse could close it, or open a second, and the pilots' monopoly would end with it.

hardConstraints: tidal; passable only at low water

preferences.neighbourRelation: a shortcut that halves a journey, on a schedule

vibe.palette: Black water, root brown, green tunnel light.

places.name: Bright-Throat Village

why.occupantsMotive: Diplomacy and craft. Their Listening-Tree and its chimes are why other tribes come to them rather than the reverse.
why.pressures: Everyone in Murkmire wants Bright-Throat's endorsement, which makes neutrality expensive to maintain.

places.name: Cold Light

places.name: The Collections Bond

places.name: New-Root

why.founding: A village founded around a cutting taken after Umbriel, by households from three stripped villages who had nothing else in common.
why.siteAdvantages: A raised hammock above the flood with good drainage — chosen for the cutting's sake, not the people's.
why.occupantsMotive: Everything here is a hundred and fifty years old at most, including the customs, and they know it.
why.pressures: The cutting is still young; if it fails, three villages' worth of memory fails with it.
why.wouldChangeIf: The tree reaching maturity would settle the village's status and end an argument with its neighbours about precedence.

hardConstraints: channel bank or spring, always with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage

vibe.palette: Pale young bark, new timber, bright green.
vibe.signatureFeature: A young Hist barely thicker than a person, inside a stockade far larger than it needs, built for the tree it will become.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): a stronger in-region 'hist-village' stays active at 'ashroot-village'.

places.name: Root-Sakka

why.founding: A Murkmire village whose tree speaks clearly and often, which makes it the region's arbiter whether it wants to be or not.
why.siteAdvantages: A river terrace on the Keel-Sakka with deep root-water and a defensible bend.
why.occupantsMotive: Their tree-minder is consulted from three days' travel away, which is a burden the village debates constantly.
why.pressures: Lilmoth's tree does not speak to anyone but its minders; this one speaks to everybody, and the comparison is politically loaded.
why.wouldChangeIf: If their tree fell silent the region would lose its only uncontested voice.

hardConstraints: channel bank or spring, always with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage

vibe.silhouette: A closed ring of roofs facing inward, so from outside the village shows you only its backs and its tree.
vibe.palette: Deep green canopy, pale plank, red-brown thatch.
vibe.materials: Mud-mother plaster and reed thatch on a hardwood frame; a laid speaking-floor of white-worn plank, argonian lamp-cages on the ring.
vibe.signatureFeature: A village built as a ring facing inward at its tree, with a speaking-floor of laid planks worn white by generations of listeners.
vibe.condition: Old, tight and well kept; the speaking-floor is renewed plank by plank and never all at once.
vibe.approach: From the river only the outward-facing backs of the ring read, and one gap that is the way in.
vibe.senses: Root-hum through the plank floor, listeners breathing, river water at the bend, sap-sweet air.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 592 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: Keelhall

why.founding: A merchantman driven ashore in a storm and never refloated; the village that gathered around it roofed it instead.
why.siteAdvantages: High on the strand above the tide, with a whole hull's worth of dry seasoned timber already in place.
why.occupantsMotive: A shore family who charge for a dry night and sell salvaged fittings out of the stern.
why.pressures: The hull is two hundred years old and the keel is going; the roof is reed and the walls are ship.
why.wouldChangeIf: When the keel finally breaks, the hall becomes a boat-shaped ruin and the family moves inland.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a shipping approach or a hazard

vibe.palette: Silvered oak, reed gold, sand.
vibe.signatureFeature: An upturned hull as a longhouse, with the sternpost carved into a door frame and light coming in where the gunports were.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance: type 'wreck' runs 9 province-wide against a countBand of 5-6, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: The Quiet Tap

why.founding: An unlicensed sap camp working a wild Hist-kin stand well inside the jungle belt, where nobody with authority goes.
why.siteAdvantages: Four hours from any village, on a stand nobody has claimed, with water to move the barrels out.
why.occupantsMotive: Sap sells for more in Lilmoth than anything else the jungle produces, and the buyers do not ask.
why.pressures: The tappers are not Argonian-local and do not know what they are doing to the stand.
why.wouldChangeIf: Discovery by any village tree-minder would end it violently.

preferences.neighbourRelation: at an isolated or rogue Hist, far from a village

vibe.palette: Amber sap, iron black, deep green.
vibe.signatureFeature: Tapped trunks with crude iron spiles and stacked barrels under a leaf roof, in a stand where every other tree is untouched.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

places.name: Chuxeth

why.founding: A tribe that never left its xanmeer, and therefore holds the strongest fortification in southern Murkmire without having built anything.
why.siteAdvantages: Stone walls, a single water approach, and ancient defences that still work — in a region where everything else is timber.
why.occupantsMotive: They are polite, immovable, and entirely uninterested in Lilmoth's politics or the An-Xileel's.
why.pressures: Every faction in the south has wanted their walls at some point; the working defences are why none has taken them.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the vakka mechanisms ever failed, the village would be ordinary overnight.

preferences.neighbourRelation: dominates its immediate district

notableNpcSlots: clan speaker on the third terrace

vibe.silhouette: A stepped stone pyramid — the only hard geometric mass above the canopy in the district — softened by washing lines and roof-awnings on every terrace.
vibe.palette: Warm grey stone, bright cloth, black scorch marks.
vibe.materials: Xanmeer tileset stone throughout, never re-cut; Argonian cane, cloth and reed added to it as fittings only, hung and lashed, never bonded.
vibe.signatureFeature: A living village on the terraces of a stepped stone pyramid, with washing lines between carved lintels and a discharge-scarred approach causeway.
vibe.condition: Ancient and fully occupied — the stone is unrepaired because it needs none, the timber on it is replaced yearly.
vibe.approach: The only stone silhouette in the district; it reads above the canopy from two directions.
vibe.senses: Voices carrying off stone, which happens nowhere else here; the discharge-crackle of the defences at night; cooking smoke, dry stone dust.

localStateVariants.description: The approach defences have been used; the causeway is scorched and the clan is not receiving.

places.whySiteWon: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 154 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: Xel-Nahkta

why.founding: A village in the jungle belt that has refused every outside contact since 4E 48 and enforces the refusal at the boundary.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible rise with one approach, three days from Lilmoth and unreachable by water.
why.occupantsMotive: They lost a village to something that came from outside and have drawn the obvious conclusion.
why.pressures: Their boundary now crosses a route the guides need, and the guides have started going around.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single successful parley would open the shortest route across the belt.

hardConstraints: defensible approach, often a single crossing

preferences.neighbourRelation: has an enemy; the enemy's ground is nearby

vibe.silhouette: A hard totem line across the approach and, behind it, roofs deliberately kept below the treeline so nothing shows from any distance.
vibe.palette: Ochre totem paint, deep green, dark timber.
vibe.materials: Mud-mother plaster and dark hardwood, one xanmeer-stone platform reused as a meeting floor, ochre-painted boundary posts, stockade timber.
vibe.signatureFeature: A totem boundary line with fresh offerings and fresh spear-marks on the same posts, and no path beyond it.
vibe.condition: Kept sharp: the boundary is renewed constantly, the village behind it looks older and less anxious.
vibe.approach: A single climbing path, one totem line across it, and no path beyond — the boundary IS the approach.
vibe.senses: Silence held on purpose; the totem line's cord-and-shell rattles in wind; ochre paint, wet leaf, no cooking smoke during daylight.

places.whySiteWon: isthmus in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 745 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: Ixtaxh Xanmeer

why.founding: The xanmeer the An-Xileel pumped out room by room and held dry with magicks; with them gone the magicks lapsed and the silt returned.
why.siteAdvantages: Sits in standing water west of Lilmoth; only the topmost chamber stands above the silt, exactly as canon first found it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody tends it. Divers go in for what the An-Xileel left behind when the water came back fast.
why.pressures: The lower rooms are silt, not water — a diver can enter them and not find the way out.
why.wouldChangeIf: Another pumping effort would reopen it, and there is no faction left with the will or the singing to do it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in drowned country; often near a drowned village

vibe.silhouette: One square of masonry in an empty sheet of water, with a rusted iron gantry still bolted across its lintel.
vibe.palette: Grey silt water, wet stone, orange rust.
vibe.materials: Xanmeer stone below silt, iron pumping gear and its timber cradle above it — the newest thing on the site by a thousand years and the most decayed.
vibe.signatureFeature: One stone chamber standing clear of flat water, with the pumping gear of a fanatical state party still bolted to its lintel and rusting.
vibe.condition: Chamber intact, machinery ruined; the party that came to drain it left everything where it stood.
vibe.approach: A single square of masonry in an otherwise empty sheet of water.
vibe.senses: Flat water noise, iron ticking as it heats, rust and silt; underwater, complete silence and the stone's ordered edges going down.

places.whySiteWon: islet in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 846 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: The Sakka Fall

why.founding: The Keel-Sakka drops nine metres over a rock lip, and has cut a chamber behind the fall.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry chamber behind falling water: hidden, cool and audible from half a kilometre.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody permanently. It has been a shrine, a cache and a hiding place in that order and probably again.
why.pressures: The chamber floods when the river rises, which is roughly when people most want to hide in it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A change in the river's course would empty and expose it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a river with real relief — the rim and upland only

vibe.palette: White water, black wet rock, green light.
vibe.signatureFeature: A curtain of water with a dry room behind it, its back wall covered in overlapping marks left by everyone who ever sheltered there.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance: type 'waterfall-chamber' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: Sakka Head

why.founding: The furthest point a loaded canoe can reach up the Keel-Sakka, and only in the wet season; in the dry it is two kilometres downstream.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock sill that is a rapid in the wet and a dry step in the dry, with a level bank for stacking cargo.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters take over here, and their season is defined entirely by where the head of navigation is this month.
why.pressures: The moving head means the porter yard is rebuilt twice a year and nobody will build anything permanent.
why.wouldChangeIf: Cutting the sill would push navigation four kilometres further in and destroy the porters' trade.

preferences.neighbourRelation: the hinge between a boat lane and a land route; a mandatory node

vibe.palette: Wet rock, stacked crate, brown flood water.
vibe.signatureFeature: A stacking bank with two abandoned upstream yards visible from it, marking where the head of navigation stood in wetter years.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): a stronger in-region 'head-of-navigation' stays active at 'head-of-tide'.

places.name: Keel-Sakka Landing

why.founding: The first village up the Keel-Sakka river from Lilmoth, where the rainforest road meets poling water.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm channel edge with deep water alongside, on the road out of Lilmoth's north gate.
why.occupantsMotive: They take Lilmoth's freight off the road and put it on the river, and charge for the change of medium.
why.pressures: Bright-Throat's chime-relay reaches here and Lilmoth's writ does not, which suits everyone locally.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cart road up the river would end the village's whole function.

hardConstraints: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed

preferences.neighbourRelation: strung along a waterway, linear not radial

vibe.silhouette: One long horizontal deck line on legs along a single bank, with canoe hulls racked overhead like a second roof.
vibe.palette: Green river, pale deck timber, red-brown thatch.
vibe.materials: Stilt-house frames of lashed hardwood, cane decking, reed thatch, argonian lamps at the deck edge; the loading deck is the only sawn timber.
vibe.signatureFeature: A single line of stilt houses along one bank with a continuous loading deck under them and canoes racked overhead.
vibe.condition: Working and rough-repaired — the deck is replaced constantly, the houses only when they fail.
vibe.approach: From the river road you walk out onto the deck and are in the village before you have entered a building.
vibe.senses: Continuous unloading, pole and hull knock, river running under the floor, fish drying, wet cordage.

places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 2), 101 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: Black Fin Grove

why.founding: A grove kept for Keshu the Black Fin, Murkmire's national hero — a hero-Hist grove is what a village does with a person it cannot let go of.
why.siteAdvantages: A stand of old Hist-kin trees on the ground where the story says she mustered, with a spring at the centre.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by rota from four villages, none of which will concede that the grove is any one of theirs.
why.pressures: The story has four incompatible versions and the rota is how the villages avoid resolving it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A definitive account would give the grove to one village and start a feud.

hardConstraints: spring or still water at the root

preferences.neighbourRelation: a regional centre; routes converge on it

notableNpcSlots: keeper of one of the four racks

vibe.silhouette: A close stand of old crowns with one pale muster-stone visible at ground level through the trunks, and four offering racks placed so that no two are ever in the same view.
vibe.palette: Deep shade, moss, four different cloth colours.
vibe.materials: Living trees and moss; one dressed muster-stone; four racks of four different woods and four different cloths, none touching, no shared structure at all.
vibe.signatureFeature: A grove of old trees with a muster-stone at its centre, and four separate offering-racks around it that never touch.
vibe.condition: Reverently maintained by four parties who will not maintain anything jointly — four immaculate racks and one neglected path.
vibe.approach: Off the path with no marker; you find it because the light drops and the ground clears.
vibe.senses: Deep shade cool, spring water, four different incenses on separate air; footsteps that everyone lowers their voice for.

heroHist.note: Register grove of hero rank, but NOT one of the ten power slots — reserve. Kept as a record and a swap candidate if the owner wants a Murkmire slot instead of one of the ten.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 624 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: The Moorings

why.founding: Households who could not get shore rights near Soulrest built on water instead, where nobody could charge them ground rent.
why.siteAdvantages: A sheltered inner lagoon with two metres of still water and mooring posts already driven for the salt trade.
why.occupantsMotive: Rent-free living in sight of the city; the mooring fee is a fraction of a shore plot.
why.pressures: The council has twice tried to tax the moorings and twice failed to define them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A legal definition of a mooring as a dwelling would end it.

hardConstraints: floats; needs sheltered water and mooring points

preferences.neighbourRelation: has two or three fixed moorings keyed to the flood cycle

vibe.palette: Wet timber, laundry colour, still green water.
vibe.signatureFeature: Twenty platform houses moored in a loose ring, with the gaps between them used as streets by canoe.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance: type 'raft-village' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 2-3, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: Lighter Flotilla

why.founding: Canon: Lilmoth is built over shallow water and large ships cannot dock, so goods are lightered ashore — and the lighter crews live afloat, between the anchorage and the quay.
why.siteAdvantages: A permanent moored ground in the estuary, half a mile off the quay, out of the tariff line and inside the sheltered water.
why.occupantsMotive: The crews control the only link between deep-water hulls and the city, and they know precisely what that is worth.
why.pressures: A council attempt to license lightering triggered a two-week stoppage that nobody wants to repeat.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dredged deep-water channel would end both the flotilla and the city's leverage over its own trade.

hardConstraints: sheltered saltwater with a reef or bar

preferences.neighbourRelation: trades with a shore settlement it does not live in

vibe.silhouette: A floating street: forty hull-lines and forty stepped masts at the same height, moving together, half a mile off the quay.
vibe.palette: Tarred hulls, bright laundry, brown estuary.
vibe.materials: Tarred working hulls with their cargo rigs still stepped, plank gangways between them, canvas roofing, argonian lamps hung in the shrouds — no fixed structure whatsoever.
vibe.signatureFeature: Forty working boats permanently moored as houses in a floating street, each with its cargo rig still stepped and its washing between the shrouds.
vibe.condition: Every hull working and none of them seaworthy; maintained exactly to the standard that keeps them afloat and no further. The flotilla is authored as a fixed moored ground, not a moving surface — hulls rise and fall with the water level, they do not carry the player anywhere.
vibe.mood: Independent, unionised in all but name.
vibe.approach: From the quay it reads as a moored fleet until you see the washing and realise nothing is going anywhere.
vibe.senses: Everything knocking against everything else all night, laundry snapping, cooking on deck, tar and bilge and estuary.

localStateVariants.description: The crews have stopped lightering; laden hulls are lying off Lilmoth doing nothing.

places.whySiteWon: river mouth in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 6 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: Lilmoth

why.founding: Rebuilt after the Slaughter of 4E 48 on the best natural harbour of the south coast, smaller and lower than the city it replaced.
why.siteAdvantages: A river estuary into Oliis Bay over shallow water; big hulls anchor out and lighter in, which is the whole economy.
why.occupantsMotive: A reconstituted merchant council governs by tariff; nobody wants a ruler, and the last party that had one killed the city.
why.pressures: Politically hostile to the An-Xileel successor state; commercially essential to a bay that must trade somewhere; built over its own mass grave.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the third Hist ever spoke to one faction alone, every institution here would break at once — which is why the rules forbid it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: bay port with a second door (a floating port) across the water
preferences.densityGradient: city core; the densest civil gradient in the south

vibe.silhouette: A stepped mass of platform-decks and stilt-towers rising in three tiers out of flat water, its skyline all verticals and washing-lines, broken by one squat Imperial gate-tower the rebuilders could not pull down.
vibe.palette: Wet grey timber, mould green, gold lamp-light in the upper walkways; below, still black water.
vibe.materials: Argonian throughout above the waterline: lashed stilt timber, split-cane decking, mud-and-reed infill, thatch and hide awnings, argonian lamp-cages. The Imperial ashlar is only what the water left standing, and nothing new is built into it.
vibe.signatureFeature: Ninety per cent Argonian stilt-and-platform work climbing high over drowned Imperial villas, inside a wall that is Imperial on three sides and Argonian facing the estuary.
vibe.condition: Rebuilt, and everywhere visibly newer than the ground it stands on: bright deck timber over black Imperial masonry, with the joins left honest.
vibe.approach: From the bay the upper platforms and the lamp-tiers read first, stacked and glowing; the drowned quarter under them only when you are inside the wall.
vibe.senses: Pole-thump and hull-knock under every walkway, the tariff bell over the quay, tar and fish-oil and drying mould, and at night the smell of wet stone rising off the drowned quarter under the floor.

places.complexityJustification: A major city on stilts over a drowned predecessor: two vertical layers, a walled circuit, a tended Hist and a repopulated slum. Compiled from the blueprint schema.

heroHist.note: Hero Hist 3/10. CANON_EXPLICIT: Lilmoth possesses its own Hist despite having no native tribe. This is the THIRD tree, grown after 4E 48 from a root fragment of the second. Young and watched: feared and tended anyway (hist-placement.md §4) — the minder's post rotates, a second tender is always present, and no faction may claim exclusive access.

localStateVariants.description: Council tariffs raised: Meerhleel and Moonmarch busy, Lilmoth quay half idle.
The third Hist has not spoken for a season; the council rules are suspended and the city is tense.
Wet-season peak: the lower walkways are closed and everything moves one tier up.

places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'lilmoth' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

places.name: The Beast Ground

why.founding: Livestock cannot go inside a stilt city, so the beast market is outside the north gate on the only firm ground.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry, level and fenced, with water on one side and the road on the other.
why.occupantsMotive: Guar, lizard-steeds, pen-bred crocodiles and hatchling stock, sold by tribes who will not enter the walls.
why.pressures: Half the sellers refuse city coin and the money-changers who solve that take a cut of every animal sold.
why.wouldChangeIf: A city livestock tariff would move the market to Alten Meerhleel overnight.

hardConstraints: a landing, because most goods come by water

preferences.neighbourRelation: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement

vibe.palette: Dust ochre, hide colours, red pen-paint.
vibe.signatureFeature: A stockade of numbered pens on firm ground outside a city that has no ground, loud from dawn, empty by dusk.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

places.name: The Cane Yard

why.founding: A city that lighters everything and poles the rest needs more canoes than any other place in the province, and builds them here.
why.siteAdvantages: On the water's edge with a steam pit, a bending frame and reed beds within poling distance.
why.occupantsMotive: Three yards' worth of families working one shore, competing on hull shape and cooperating on materials.
why.pressures: Good cane is coming from further away every year as the near beds are over-cut.
why.wouldChangeIf: A reed-bed failure would raise the price of every hull in the bay.

preferences.neighbourRelation: serves a port or a water-village cluster

vibe.palette: Pale cane, black lacquer, steam white.
vibe.signatureFeature: Rows of half-built hulls on trestles at every stage from bent frame to lacquered finish, under one continuous open roof.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance: type 'boatwright-yard' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: Under-Yard

why.founding: Lilmoth stands on a drowned city and salvage from underneath it is a licensed, taxed, entirely respectable trade.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay directly above the deepest of the sunken villas, with a stair down to a landing at water level.
why.occupantsMotive: Crews work the drowned quarter by permit, in pairs, and hand everything to the yard for valuation.
why.pressures: Some of what comes up belongs to families still living, and the yard has to decide that daily.
why.wouldChangeIf: A find of An-Xileel material would turn a trade into a political incident.

preferences.neighbourRelation: always paired with drowned ground it works

notableNpcSlots: valuer who does not ask where things came from

vibe.silhouette: A low open-sided valuation floor at the quay edge with a black stair-mouth going straight down out of it into the water.
vibe.palette: Black mould, tarnished silver, green water light.
vibe.materials: Quay stone below, scaffold-and-canvas above, drip-racks and lot-tables of scrubbed plank; submerged Imperial masonry visible through the stair-mouth.
vibe.signatureFeature: A valuation floor of mould-blackened Imperial household goods laid out in lots, dripping, with a diving stair going straight down into the city.
vibe.condition: Busy and grim, everything stained black to the same height by the same water.
vibe.approach: From the quay lane it is one more open shed until you see what is laid out on the tables.
vibe.senses: Dripping, constant; the mould smell of drowned houses brought up into daylight; scrubbing brushes; a bell rung for each diver surfacing.

localStateVariants.description: The council has taken the valuation book; the floor is empty and the stair is chained.

places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 2), 55 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: The Weighing Room

why.founding: Where the merchant council's tariff is actually applied, argued and evaded, one lot at a time.
why.siteAdvantages: On the lighter quay, between the water stair and the warehouse row.
why.occupantsMotive: Council clerks, lighter captains and brokers in one room, which is deliberate.
why.pressures: Foreigners were once restricted to the docks by law; the law lapsed and the habit did not.
why.wouldChangeIf: A formal foreign quarter inside the wall would empty this room of half its business.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement

vibe.palette: Brass and chalk, wet plank, lamp gold.
vibe.signatureFeature: A public scale under a lantern with the day's tariff chalked beside it, and three separate sets of books being kept at the same table.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): a stronger in-region 'tradehouse' stays active at 'soulrest-quay-tradehouse'.

places.name: Long Bar

why.founding: A shoal bar off the salvage coast where a false light has been shown for longer than anyone will admit.
why.siteAdvantages: Two miles of breaking bar on the Southern Sea approach, invisible from the coast road, hidden from Soulrest by the islands.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvage families who decided that waiting for wrecks was inefficient; they take the low-profile Southern Sea traders nobody reports missing.
why.pressures: Khajiit crews keep the same lane and have begun to notice; the Soulrest harbour office would have to act if it were ever proved.
why.wouldChangeIf: A working lighthouse on the headland would end it in one season.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a shipping approach with reefs or bars

notableNpcSlots: light-keeper who is not a light-keeper

vibe.silhouette: Nothing by day but a stilted driftwood frame on an empty beach; by night, a single light where a light should not be.
vibe.palette: Black wet shingle, salt-white bone, tarred rope.
vibe.materials: Driftwood, salvaged spar and cordage, a stone-weighted pyre frame; the only permanent structure is the sorting lots marked out in beach stone.
vibe.signatureFeature: A driftwood pyre-frame on stilts above the tide line and a beach of sorted cargo laid out in lots.
vibe.condition: Nothing built to last, everything replaced from the last wreck.

places.name: The Outside Barge

why.founding: Pusbottom's games moved onto the water when the council started raiding buildings, and never moved back.
why.siteAdvantages: Moored outside the wall line, shiftable in an hour, and reachable only by boat.
why.occupantsMotive: Dice, obligation-broking and the buying of debts; the criminal underground of a city that has always had one.
why.pressures: The council knows exactly where it is and moves against it only when a council member loses badly.
why.wouldChangeIf: A licensed gaming house inside the wall would kill it and nobody would propose one.

hardConstraints: a mooring is half the type

preferences.neighbourRelation: in a port, a market town or a slum quarter

vibe.palette: Lamp red, black water, painted deck.
vibe.signatureFeature: A lantern-lit barge with a shallow-draught tender always alongside and a bell to warn the tables.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance: type 'vice-den' runs 6 province-wide against a countBand of 4-5, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: Quin'rawl Anchorage

why.founding: Southern Sea crews — a large share of them Khajiit — keep a low profile to avoid Altmer and Maormer warships, so they anchor where no state looks.
why.siteAdvantages: A deep cove behind a headland with two exits, sand holding ground and a freshwater run at its head.
why.occupantsMotive: Half the hulls here carry a Soulrest charter, and all of them carry cargo the charter does not mention.
why.pressures: Soulrest's council both licenses and disowns them, which is a stable arrangement everyone resents.
why.wouldChangeIf: A Dominion sweep of the Southern Sea would scatter it to the mangroves in a week.

hardConstraints: deep approach, hidden from the lane

preferences.neighbourRelation: near a shipping lane it can reach and leave

notableNpcSlots: the chartered master everyone pretends not to know

vibe.silhouette: Six low mastless hull-lines in a cove under a dark headland, and one properly rigged ship anchored in the middle of them looking entirely respectable.
vibe.palette: Sailcloth ochre, wet sand, dark cliff green.
vibe.materials: Sailcloth shore-camp, beached hulls used as stores, scaffold cargo-shears, no permanent building anywhere on the beach.
vibe.signatureFeature: Six low hulls moored bow-and-stern in a cove, a shore camp of sailcloth, and a chartered ship anchored respectably among them.
vibe.condition: Camp, not settlement — everything here can be off the beach in three hours and regularly is.
vibe.approach: Neither entrance shows the anchorage until you are inside the headland; then the whole cove is in front of you at once.
vibe.senses: Rigging in the headland wind, dogs, roasting meat, fresh water running at the head of the cove, tar.

places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 439 m from the nearest route; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: Rockpark

why.founding: Canon empties Rockpark of every business and guild through pestilence, plague and a curse; nobody returned because its Hist died.
why.siteAdvantages: Good firm ground on the north-east road out of Lilmoth — which is why its emptiness is so conspicuous.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The Unearthed Equipment Store still blocks the palace gate and the palace still holds what the royal family became.
why.pressures: It is a day's walk from a living city and stocked with five centuries of untouched goods, and still nobody goes in.
why.wouldChangeIf: A confirmed cure for whatever is in the palace would strip the town in a week.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in the country the Flu emptied; other villages avoid it

vibe.silhouette: A complete town skyline with no smoke in it — every roof standing, every chimney cold, and one collapsed store jammed diagonally across the palace gate.
vibe.palette: Dust grey, faded shop-paint, black doorways.
vibe.materials: Mud-mother plaster, bamboo frame, shack-kit and wattle, all sixteen centuries weathered and none of it rebuilt; the shop paint is original.
vibe.signatureFeature: A whole town with its shop shutters closed and its stock still on the shelves, and a collapsed equipment store jammed across the palace gate.
vibe.condition: Intact and refused — preserved not by care but by a taboo nobody has broken, with the stock still on the shelves.
vibe.approach: The road runs straight into it; nothing on the road warns you, which is worse.
vibe.senses: Absolute quiet in a place built for noise; dust; doors that move in wind; no birds in the streets.

localStateVariants.description: Somebody has broken the taboo; the shelves are stripped and the district knows who.

places.whySiteWon: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 269 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: The Rockpark Stump

why.founding: The reason Rockpark was never resettled: its Hist died, and with it the memory the village kept in it.
why.siteAdvantages: The town's central enclosure, still walled, still swept by pilgrims who come and do not stay.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. Tree-minders from three villages visit annually and take nothing.
why.pressures: A dead Hist's mnemic egg is a theological emergency nobody in the region wants to be responsible for.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cutting taking root here would change Murkmire's whole map of who is owed what.

preferences.neighbourRelation: beside a bereaved or sap-touched village

vibe.palette: Ash-grey wood, green wall moss, bright offering cloth.
vibe.signatureFeature: A hollow grey stump inside a maintained wall, with offerings placed on its rim by people who then leave immediately.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance: type 'harmed-hist' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: Under-Root

why.founding: A walkable gallery under a great root mass, dry above the flood, and occupied by people who wanted somewhere no one would look.
why.siteAdvantages: Two hundred metres of natural passage with three entrances and a permanent air flow.
why.occupantsMotive: Whoever is currently in it — the tenancy changes and the fittings do not.
why.pressures: The gallery floods to chest height in the deep wet season, on about a week's notice.
why.wouldChangeIf: A root collapse would close the middle and split it into two dead ends.

hardConstraints: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded

preferences.neighbourRelation: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect, and that connection is the map

vibe.silhouette: A living tunnel mouth at the base of a root buttress, breathing warm air, with three worn approaches converging on it.
vibe.palette: Root brown, soot black, green entrance light.
vibe.materials: Living root as wall, floor and ceiling; three tenancies' worth of cut niches and hearth-scars at three heights; lamp brackets driven into wood, never stone.
vibe.signatureFeature: A living tunnel of root with hearth-scars and shelf niches cut into it at three different heights by three different tenancies.
vibe.condition: Continuously reoccupied for centuries, with each tenancy's alterations cut across the last one's.
vibe.approach: The through-draught is the cue — you feel warm air on the path before you see the mouth.
vibe.senses: A permanent through-draught that is warm at one end and cold at the other; soot; sap; the root-hum under bare feet.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 200 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on route, region, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: Customs Suburb

why.founding: The Imperial customs suburb outside Lilmoth's north gate, looted by the An-Xileel when they took the city from the Empire.
why.siteAdvantages: Astride the north road where every cargo had to pass, which is why it was built and why it was sacked.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody rebuilt it; Lilmoth's rebuilt council collects at the quay instead and prefers not to be reminded.
why.pressures: Its record room survived the fire and nobody has read it in two centuries.
why.wouldChangeIf: The records would establish who owned what before 4E 48, which several families would prefer stayed unknown.

hardConstraints: in a port or a city

preferences.neighbourRelation: attached to a living settlement that does not talk about it

vibe.silhouette: A street of roofless Imperial gables with the road still running dead straight through them, and one intact vaulted roof at the end of it.
vibe.palette: Fire-black render, red brick core, green regrowth.
vibe.materials: Fire-blacked render over red brick core, fallen pantile, iron window grilles; no Argonian material anywhere — nobody has moved in.
vibe.signatureFeature: A burnt street of Imperial offices with the road still running through it, and one vaulted record room with an intact roof.
vibe.condition: Burnt and left: structurally dangerous, deliberately unrepaired, with two centuries of green established inside every room.
vibe.approach: The north road takes you straight down its middle; the record room's intact roof is the only thing that reads as whole.
vibe.senses: Wind through open windows, regrowth cracking render, wet ash smell that has never quite gone, and the road noise from beyond it.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 55 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: The Drying House

why.founding: Lilmoth's sap trade produced enough people who could not stop that the villages built somewhere to put them.
why.siteAdvantages: Outside the city, upwind, beside running water, with no sap within a day's walk in any direction.
why.occupantsMotive: Run by former users; the treatment is time, water, work and the absence of any supply.
why.pressures: The city's dealers know exactly where it is and one of them funds it, which nobody can decide how to feel about.
why.wouldChangeIf: Closing the illicit taps in the jungle would empty the house in five years.

preferences.neighbourRelation: just outside a settlement, near sap country

vibe.palette: Whitewash, rope hemp, running water.
vibe.signatureFeature: A long dormitory hall with barred windows facing away from the city, and a work yard of rope-making that never stops.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

places.name: Screen-Watch

why.founding: A village of the people who pilot Bramman's river, built inside the mangrove wall a mile above its mouth.
why.siteAdvantages: Invisible from the bay; every house sits on the channel it watches; the mangrove is both wall and roof.
why.occupantsMotive: Piloting fees, and a strict internal rule that no two families ever teach the same reach of the river.
why.pressures: Blackguards want the river as a road, Soulrest wants it as a customs problem, and the village wants it to stay a rumour.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the channel were ever charted publicly the village would have no reason to exist.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately not on any lane

vibe.silhouette: None. The mangrove wall is unbroken from the bay and the village exists entirely inside it.
vibe.palette: Root black, leaf green, pale lashed cordage.
vibe.materials: Decking cut between living trunks, lashed and never nailed into the tree; shack-kit walls, cane, hanging canoe slings.
vibe.signatureFeature: Platforms cut into the mangrove wall itself, decked between living trunks, with poled canoes hanging in slings above the tide.
vibe.condition: Kept invisible — no cut lines to the water, no smoke above the canopy, decking stained to match the root.
vibe.approach: You are inside it before you see it.
vibe.senses: Bay noise heard but not seen; canoes creaking in their slings; leaf and root black-water smell; people who do not raise their voices.

places.whySiteWon: water narrows in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 726 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, parent, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: Shut-From-Within

why.founding: Sealed by its own people when its Hist chamber was emptied, so that whatever remains inside stays inside.
why.siteAdvantages: A low xanmeer on a rise, unremarkable except that its door was closed from within.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing tends it. Its traps are intact and its Hist chamber is not empty in the way the sealers believed.
why.pressures: Two villages disagree about which of them did the sealing, and therefore about who may open it.
why.wouldChangeIf: An agreement between the two villages would open it legitimately for the first time in centuries.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately hard to reach; no village tends it

vibe.silhouette: A low stone step-mass barely clearing the scrub, with one dark vertical seam in it that reads wrong from any angle.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, ochre mortar, black seam.
vibe.materials: Xanmeer stone and ornament, and one course of ochre mortar laid by hand from the inside — the only non-original material on the structure.
vibe.signatureFeature: A stone door closed from the inside, with the sealing crew's hand-marks still in the mortar around it.
vibe.condition: Perfectly sound and completely closed; the hand-marks in the mortar are as sharp as the day they were pressed.
vibe.approach: Unremarkable until you are close enough to see that the door was closed from the wrong side.
vibe.senses: Nothing. No draught at the seam, no water sound, no insects on that face of the stone; the silence is the reason people come.

localStateVariants.description: The seal is broken; whatever was closed in is a district-wide problem.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 471 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: The Shut Door

why.founding: Closed deliberately by its own people at some point after the Duskfall and never reopened; the mechanisms were left live.
why.siteAdvantages: On a low rise in the burn country, far enough from any village that its closure was a decision, not an abandonment.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living tends it. The vakka-stone defences still hold charge.
why.pressures: Two treasure crews have gone in this generation and neither came out, which has done more for its security than the traps.
why.wouldChangeIf: A discharge of the vakka stones would open the whole complex at once.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately hard to reach; no village tends it

vibe.palette: Cold grey stone, scorch black, blue-white spark.
vibe.signatureFeature: A perfectly fitted stone door with no handle and a discharge-scar fanned across the terrace in front of it.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): a stronger in-region 'sealed-xanmeer' stays active at 'sealed-meer-murkmire'.

places.name: The Slaughter Ground

why.founding: Where Lilmoth buried the dead of 4E 48 — its own residents, killed first, by their own city's tree and its party.
why.siteAdvantages: Outside the rebuilt wall on the only firm ground large enough, because inside the wall is the mass grave the city stands on.
why.occupantsMotive: A rotating vigil, maintained by the same rule as the tree-minders': never one faction, never one person.
why.pressures: The An-Xileel successor state denies the causation; Lilmoth's whole civic identity depends on it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A reconciliation with the successor state would require abandoning the inscription, and it will not happen.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village

notableNpcSlots: wall-cutter who refuses to fill the blank section

vibe.silhouette: A long low wall running across open ground with one tended tree behind it — horizontal where everything else in the district is vertical.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, cut-shadow, one green tended tree.
vibe.materials: Cut grey stone, three scripts, one deliberately unfinished blank section; wattle enclosure and one planted tree.
vibe.signatureFeature: A long low wall with names cut into it in three scripts, and a single unnamed section left blank for the ones nobody could count.
vibe.condition: Immaculate, and politically maintained — the blank section is re-cut clean every year rather than filled.
vibe.approach: From the gate road the wall reads as a low line with the city behind it, which is the intended comparison.
vibe.senses: Reading aloud; the city audible over the wall and not visible; cut grass; offerings.

places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 1), 67 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: The Smoulder Cuts

why.founding: Peat is the district's only fuel now the timber is gone, and it is cut on the edge of ground that is already alight underneath.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep dry peat, cuttable in the dry season, close enough to the coast road to sell.
why.occupantsMotive: Cutters work the cool face and race the fire; a cut worked out before the fire arrives is a good year.
why.pressures: The fire moves underground at walking pace and cannot be seen; two cutters were lost last season.
why.wouldChangeIf: Wet-season flooding could quench the whole seam and end both the danger and the fuel.

preferences.neighbourRelation: in the burn country, or supplying a village's fires

vibe.palette: Chocolate peat brown, blue smoke, scorched orange.
vibe.signatureFeature: Stacked drying peats in neat rows with a haze of smoke coming out of the ground fifty paces behind them.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

places.name: Soulrest

why.founding: Third-Era provincial capital at the one sheltered deep-water landfall where Topal Bay meets the Southern Sea.
why.siteAdvantages: Peninsula wrapping the bay; a river mouth just south opening a route north-east into the interior; islands screening the approach.
why.occupantsMotive: Four powers hold pieces of it: a merchant council, an orphaned Imperial apparatus, interior tribes, and the river interests who control Bramman's water.
why.pressures: Its gold-and-timber hinterland was burned by the tribes in 3E 427 and never rebuilt; the capital moved; the offices remain, administering nothing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the mines reopened, or if one of the four claimants finally won, the city would stop being a stalemate and start being a capital again.

hardConstraints: bay port at a concealed river's mouth

preferences.neighbourRelation: controls a hidden navigable channel inland
preferences.densityGradient: city core; the province's second densest civil gradient

notableNpcSlots: orphaned Imperial magistrate (no jurisdiction, full procedure)
tribal delegate lodging in the palace

vibe.silhouette: A long low limestone palace roof and a customs campanile on a peninsula spine, with a ragged secondary skyline of Argonian and Khajiit roofs growing out of and over the Imperial one.
vibe.palette: Salt-bleached limestone and grey weathered timber under wet green mould; Khajiit awning colour in the dock lanes.
vibe.materials: Two kits standing side by side and never blended: Imperial salt-cut limestone, pantile and iron-strapped door in the administrative shell; lashed timber, reed thatch and painted Khajiit awning cloth in the town that grew through it.
vibe.signatureFeature: An Imperial administrative shell — palace, courthouse, bonded stores — with an Argonian and Khajiit town grown through and over it, sea-noise stopping dead at the gate.
vibe.condition: Structurally sound and functionally hollow: every roof kept, half the rooms unused, weeds established in the ceremonial pavement and nowhere else.
vibe.approach: From the coast road the palace roof and the campanile read first, together; the harbour is only visible past the mole.
vibe.senses: Sea noise that stops dead at the gate, gulls in the mole, four languages in the dock lanes, mould and old paper in the arcades, spice smoke from the Khajiit quarter.

places.complexityJustification: A major city: districts, walls, a harbour and four competing authorities. Compiled from the settlement blueprint schema, not hand-placed geometry.

localStateVariants.description: One of the four claimants is briefly on top; the gates and the harbour office change hands with it.
A survey party is in town and the whole city is behaving as if the mines might reopen.

places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'soulrest' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

places.name: Breaking Hard

why.founding: Where the Expeditionary Force's transports were cut up for their iron when the Empire stopped paying for them.
why.siteAdvantages: A hard shingle slope inside the mole with deep water at its foot — the only place on the coast a hull can be laid over.
why.occupantsMotive: Breakers who make more from Imperial fastenings than any local trade makes from anything.
why.pressures: The supply of Imperial hulls is finite and nearly finished; the yard has started buying wrecks off the Long Bar and asking nothing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Soulrest ever built ships again, the same slope would serve.

preferences.neighbourRelation: one per major port; the whole coast's hulls come from a handful of these

vibe.silhouette: Half a warship's ribcage standing in the shallows, dominating the harbour skyline more than anything still afloat in it.
vibe.palette: Iron-orange, tar black, sun-silvered oak.
vibe.materials: Sun-silvered oak frames, iron fastenings stacked by size, tar, scaffold shears and a shingle hard; sorted timber lots run the length of the beach.
vibe.signatureFeature: Half a warship's ribcage standing in the shallows, being unmade plank by plank into stacked, sorted, sellable pieces.
vibe.condition: Perpetually mid-demolition — there has been a hull being unmade here continuously for eighty years.
vibe.approach: The ribcage reads from inside the mole as a ship until you notice which way the planks are coming off.
vibe.senses: Adze and maul all day, iron ringing, tar boiling, bilge water, sawdust that smells of somewhere else.

places.whySiteWon: cove in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 61 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, parent, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: The Broken Bond

why.founding: Imperial customs bond for gold and timber exports; sealed in 3E 427 when the exports stopped and opened by hand shortly after.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay, behind the harbour office, with its own water gate for lighters.
why.occupantsMotive: Squatters, a bond-clerk's descendant who still keeps the ledger, and whoever needs dry floor space this month.
why.pressures: The ledger records cargo that no longer exists and names families who would rather it did not.
why.wouldChangeIf: A council audit would turn a curiosity into a scandal.

preferences.neighbourRelation: attached to a port or a wharf

vibe.palette: Damp brick, verdigris, ledger-paper cream.
vibe.signatureFeature: Imperial iron doors levered off their hinges and stacked neatly inside, as if the theft had been an official act.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance: type 'bonded-warehouse' runs 7 province-wide against a countBand of 4-6, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: Soulrest Poling Relay

why.founding: A relay post where letters and small freight change from road carriage to poled canoe for the interior river.
why.siteAdvantages: At the river's head of tide, where the coast road first touches navigable water.
why.occupantsMotive: Polers work fixed reaches and hand over; nobody carries a letter more than a day from home.
why.pressures: Letters to the interior are read by three different interests before they arrive and everyone knows it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single through-carrier service would be faster and instantly less trusted.

preferences.neighbourRelation: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay

vibe.palette: Wet cane, letter cream, river brown.
vibe.signatureFeature: A rack of numbered canoes under a long roof and a board of destination pegs that is the closest thing the district has to a timetable.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance: type 'courier-relay' runs 10 province-wide against a countBand of 7-9, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: The Divers' Yard

why.founding: Salvage is one of the three things Soulrest still lives on, and salvage needs a yard to land, sort and sell what comes up.
why.siteAdvantages: On the inner harbour, with a crane frame, a fresh-water rinse and the buyers' benches thirty paces away.
why.occupantsMotive: Diver crews sell by lot; the yard takes a share and asks where nothing came from.
why.pressures: Every lot on the bench is somebody's cargo; the harbour office periodically wants the books.
why.wouldChangeIf: An enforced provenance rule would collapse the trade into the Long Bar's hands.

preferences.neighbourRelation: always paired with drowned ground it works

vibe.palette: Rust, salt crust, wet rope.
vibe.signatureFeature: Sorting tables under an open roof, laid out with corroded ironwork, amphora bases and one very good thing per week.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): a stronger in-region 'salvage-divers-yard' stays active at 'lilmoth-divers-yard'.

places.name: The Low Fair

why.founding: An outside-the-wall fair that runs four times a year because interior traders will not enter Soulrest's gates and the council will not go out.
why.siteAdvantages: Level dry ground beside the coast road, a river landing on one side and the city gate on the other.
why.occupantsMotive: Everyone gets what they want without conceding anything: the tribes do not enter, the council does not leave.
why.pressures: Both sides periodically try to move the fair to their own advantage; it has not moved in eighty years.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the tribes ever entered the city freely, the fair would die and so would the arrangement.

hardConstraints: a landing, because most goods come by water

preferences.neighbourRelation: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement

vibe.palette: Tent ochre and red, trampled green, grey stone bases.
vibe.signatureFeature: A permanent grid of empty post-holes and stone stall-bases that fills with tents four times a year and is bare grass the rest of the time.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

places.name: The Governors' Ground

why.founding: Two centuries of Imperial administrators, officers and settlers buried outside Soulrest's wall in consecrated Cyrodilic form.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm dry ground just outside the gate, deliberately not in Argonian burial country.
why.occupantsMotive: Maintained by a single hereditary sexton whose family has outlasted the government that hired it.
why.pressures: Nobody has been buried here in a hundred and forty years and the ground rent has not been paid since.
why.wouldChangeIf: A council decision to build on it would be the moment Soulrest admits the Empire is gone.

preferences.neighbourRelation: attached to a foreign settlement

vibe.palette: Grey slab, moss green, raked white gravel.
vibe.signatureFeature: Rows of Nibenese name-slabs sinking at different angles in wet ground, with a swept gravel path kept perfectly clear.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance: type 'foreign-graveyard' runs 3 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: Long Table

why.founding: The quayside house where cargo is contracted, crews are hired and the council's tariffs are argued about.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay, between the harbour office and the divers' yard.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper sells information at the same table as beer and considers both a single trade.
why.pressures: Everyone who matters in the port drinks here, which makes it the least private room in the city.
why.wouldChangeIf: A council monopoly on brokerage would empty it.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement

vibe.silhouette: A wide low hall with all its shutters open to the quay and a chalked rate wall visible from outside.
vibe.palette: Beer amber, chalk white, wet-boot grey.
vibe.materials: Imperial-frontage stonework on the quay side (this is the old town), Argonian fittings inside and nothing structural crossing between them; one forty-foot table of scarfed plank.
vibe.signatureFeature: One table forty feet long with the day's freight rates chalked on the wall above it in three scripts.
vibe.condition: Hard-used and profitable — table scarred, floor worn to a channel from door to bar.
vibe.approach: You hear the rate being argued before you reach the door, which is the point of the open shutters.
vibe.senses: Loud: three languages, chalk on slate, beer, wet boots, and the harbour through the open shutters.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 16 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

places.name: The Synod Outstation

why.founding: Canon states the Synod had no presence within roughly four hundred miles of Lilmoth; this is the nearest station, and it is why.
why.siteAdvantages: Inside Soulrest's wall, on the coast, resuppliable by sea without ever entering the interior.
why.occupantsMotive: A magister and two assistants studying the burn country's ground fires, with a licence that expired long ago.
why.pressures: The council tolerates them for the fees; the interior tribes have made clear how far east they may go.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the sea supply would close the station within a season.

why.occupantsMotive: The instruments sell across the province; the village's real product is the tuning, which cannot be bought elsewhere.
why.pressures: Bright-Throat's chime craft is fashionable and this is not; young makers are leaving for the cliffs.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the hardwood stand would end the craft in a generation.

hardConstraints: landing plus access to its raw material

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a trade water; brokers between neighbours

vibe.palette: Warm wood, lacquer red, green stand.
vibe.signatureFeature: A village where every house has a drying loft of shaped wood and the whole place is tuned each morning, audibly, at once.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

places.name: Wallside

why.founding: Households pushed out of Lilmoth's tariff line built against the outside of the city wall, on platforms in the mangrove.
why.siteAdvantages: The wall itself is one side of every house; the mangrove is the other three.
why.occupantsMotive: Close enough to work in the city daily and far enough out to owe it nothing.
why.pressures: The council periodically declares the platforms a fire risk and never removes them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A wall repair programme would demolish the lot without any decision being taken.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately not on any lane

vibe.palette: Grey wall stone, raw plank, dark water.
vibe.signatureFeature: Houses built directly onto the outside face of a city wall, with ladders up to a postern the council pretends is sealed.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance (140 records against a 45-56 budget): a stronger in-region 'mangrove-platform-village' stays active at 'screen-watch'.

places.name: Charge-In-The-Water

why.founding: A wamasu nesting pond; canon has the beast curse all the water around it to deadly convulsions, which makes the pond itself the hazard.
why.siteAdvantages: A still isolated pond with a sand bank the animal returns to, and no through route past it.
why.occupantsMotive: The adult. Egg-poachers come anyway, from downstream, on foot.
why.pressures: The water within thirty metres is lethal while the adult is present, and the adult is usually present.
why.wouldChangeIf: A poached clutch would drive the adult out and free a whole channel network.

hardConstraints: a held pond, still and avoided

preferences.neighbourRelation: a district hazard; villages route around it

vibe.palette: Blue-white flicker, black water, pale sand.
vibe.signatureFeature: A pond with a hard sand nest bank, dead fish rimming the edges, and the surface twitching with light before anything is visible.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the mercantile-coast over-density rebalance: type 'wamasu-pond' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: White Rose Prison

why.founding: One of the prisons canon says the Empire built after 1E 2837, sited by the Imperial rule for this province: put it where the marsh is the wall.
why.siteAdvantages: An island of firm ground in burn-country marsh with one causeway, serving the convict-worked mines behind Soulrest.
why.occupantsMotive: Empty of the living. Full of Argonian dead who died away from their Hist and whose bones were never brought to the dirt.
why.pressures: The Blackrose Chainbreakers want the dead repatriated; the structure is sound enough that somebody will eventually want it back.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reoccupation by any armed party would make the repatriation impossible and the grievance permanent.

preferences.neighbourRelation: far from everything, by design

vibe.silhouette: A white rectangular block above reed — hard-edged, unweathered, with an intact causeway and an open gate; it reads white from a long way off.
vibe.palette: Lime white, marsh brown, black door-shadow.
vibe.materials: Imperial lime render over dressed stone, iron gate furniture, tiled roof complete; no scavenging, no Argonian addition, nothing taken.
vibe.signatureFeature: A white lime-rendered Imperial block, structurally perfect and utterly silent, standing above marsh with its causeway intact and its gate open.
vibe.condition: Structurally perfect and utterly abandoned — the render is sound, the gate is open, and nobody has taken so much as a hinge.
vibe.approach: It reads white through the reeds from a long way off — one of the few real long sightlines in the lowland.
vibe.senses: Silence with a building in it; reeds; the causeway underfoot; lime dust; no smell of occupation at all.

localStateVariants.description: The repatriation chain has finished here; the block is empty in a different way.
